questions.q: What term matches this definition: Electrostatic attraction between positively charged metal particles and delocalised electrons in a metallic lattice.
What term matches this definition: Electrons that are not attached to one particular atom and can move throughout a structure.
What term matches this definition: Bonding where attraction acts in all directions, allowing particles to shift while maintaining attraction.
What term matches this definition: Strong electrostatic attraction between positively charged cations and negatively charged anions.
What term matches this definition: A strong attraction formed when atoms share a pair of electrons.
What term matches this definition: A large continuous structure of atoms connected by strong covalent bonds.
What term matches this definition: A repeating three-dimensional arrangement of oppositely charged ions held by electrostatic attraction.
What term matches this definition: A repeating structure of positive metal particles surrounded by delocalised electrons.
What term matches this definition: Attractive forces acting between separate molecules.
What term matches this definition: Attractive forces or bonds acting between atoms within the same particle or molecule.
What term matches this definition: The ability of a solid to be hammered, bent or moulded into a different shape without breaking.
What term matches this definition: The ability of a material to be drawn into a wire without breaking.
What term matches this definition: The tendency of a material to break or shatter when sufficient force is applied.
What term matches this definition: The ability of a substance to allow charged particles to move through it and carry electrical current.
What term matches this definition: The ability of a solute to dissolve in a solvent to form a solution.
What term matches this definition: Energy associated with the attractive forces holding oppositely charged ions together within an ionic lattice.
What term matches this definition: A molecule with an uneven distribution of charge, producing regions of partial positive and negative charge.
What term matches this definition: A separation of electrical charge that creates a partially positive region and a partially negative region.
What term matches this definition: Electrons in the outer shell of an atom that are involved in chemical bonding.
What term matches this definition: A pair of valence electrons located on an atom that is not involved in a covalent bond.
What term matches this definition: A region of electron density associated with a bond between atoms.
What term matches this definition: A region around an atom where negatively charged electrons are located.
What term matches this definition: The three-dimensional arrangement of atoms around a central atom in a molecule.
What term matches this definition: A molecular arrangement involving four bonding regions around a central atom, arranged for maximum separation.
What term matches this definition: A molecular shape involving three bonding regions and one lone pair around the central atom.
What term matches this definition: An organic compound made entirely from carbon and hydrogen atoms.
What term matches this definition: A hydrocarbon in which the carbon atoms have the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms attached.
What term matches this definition: A hydrocarbon containing a carbon-carbon double or triple bond and therefore not having the maximum possible hydrogen atoms.
What term matches this definition: A saturated hydrocarbon containing only single carbon-carbon bonds.
What term matches this definition: An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond.
What term matches this definition: An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing at least one carbon-carbon triple bond.
What term matches this definition: A separation technique that separates components of a mixture according to differences in boiling point or volatility.
What term matches this definition: A measure of how readily a substance vaporises; more volatile substances enter the gas phase more easily.
What term matches this definition: A reaction where atoms are added across a multiple bond, producing a more saturated molecule.
What term matches this definition: A rule used to predict the major product when an unsymmetrical molecule is added across an unsymmetrical alkene.
What term matches this definition: The product formed in the greatest amount when a reaction can produce multiple structural products.
What term matches this definition: A possible product formed in a smaller amount than the major product.
What term matches this definition: A chemical reaction in which a fuel reacts with oxygen and releases energy.
What term matches this definition: Combustion occurring with sufficient oxygen, producing carbon dioxide and water from the fuels considered in the exam.
What term matches this definition: Combustion occurring with limited oxygen, allowing products such as carbon monoxide and carbon to form.
What term matches this definition: A chemical reaction that releases energy to the surroundings.
What term matches this definition: The energy change associated with a chemical reaction; the exam uses a negative ΔH to indicate energy release.
What term matches this definition: The principle that matter is not created or destroyed during a chemical reaction.
What term matches this definition: A system in which matter cannot escape, allowing the total mass before and after a reaction to be compared.
What term matches this definition: A reaction in which two or more reactants combine to form one product.
What term matches this definition: A reaction in which one reactant breaks down to form two or more products.
What term matches this definition: A reaction between an acid and a base that produces a salt and water.
What term matches this definition: A reaction involving soluble ionic substances that produces an insoluble solid.
What term matches this definition: An insoluble solid formed from substances reacting in solution.
What term matches this definition: A substance capable of donating hydrogen ions, H⁺, and producing a conjugate base.
What term matches this definition: An acid that fully dissociates into ions in solution.
What term matches this definition: An acid that only partially dissociates, establishing an equilibrium between ionised and unionised forms.
What term matches this definition: The process in which a substance separates into ions when in solution.
What term matches this definition: The species remaining after an acid has donated a hydrogen ion.
What term matches this definition: A condition in which forward and reverse processes occur, represented in the exam using a reversible arrow.
What term matches this definition: An acid capable of donating two hydrogen ions.
What term matches this definition: The lowering of ocean pH associated in the exam with CO₂ reacting with seawater and increasing acidity.
What term matches this definition: A measure related in the exam to the number of successful particle collisions occurring each second.
What term matches this definition: The amount of time required for a reaction to reach completion.
What term matches this definition: The idea that reacting particles must collide with sufficient energy and an appropriate orientation for a successful reaction.
What term matches this definition: A collision between reactant particles that has sufficient energy and suitable orientation to produce a reaction.
What term matches this definition: The minimum energy requirement that must be overcome for a chemical reaction to occur.
What term matches this definition: A substance that increases reaction rate by providing a pathway with a lower activation energy.
What term matches this definition: The amount of a substance present within a particular volume of solution.
What term matches this definition: The amount of a solid reactant exposed and available for collisions with other reactant particles.
What term matches this definition: A different structural form of the same chemical element in the same physical state.
What term matches this definition: A carbon allotrope consisting of covalently bonded layers with delocalised electrons and weaker attractions between layers.
What term matches this definition: A carbon allotrope consisting of a three-dimensional network of carbon atoms connected by strong covalent bonds.
What term matches this definition: A large molecule made from many smaller repeating units linked together in long chains.
What term matches this definition: A smaller molecule capable of joining with other monomers to form a polymer.
What term matches this definition: A chemical reaction in which monomers join together to form a polymer.
What term matches this definition: The structural section of a polymer that repeats throughout the polymer chain.
What term matches this definition: A manufactured polymer, such as polyethylene, Kevlar or nylon in the exam classification.
What term matches this definition: A naturally occurring polymer, such as DNA, silk or collagen in the exam classification.
